Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) – Scotland

Reporting To:
SHEQ Manager

Location:
Scotland – project based with regular travel to live construction sites

Function:
SHEQ / Environment

Role Purpose

The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Scotland.

Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with Scottish environmental legislation, planning requirements, protected species licences, client requirements and project environmental commitments.

The role will have a strong field-based component, working alongside project management, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological constraints, develop practical mitigation and provide ECoW supervision of activities in environmentally sensitive locations.

The position will be particularly important on linear power infrastructure projects where construction activities may interact with protected species, designated sites, peatland, watercourses, forestry and sensitive habitats.

Key Responsibilities

Ecological Clerk of Works

Act as ECoW for construction activities requiring ecological supervision.
Undertake pre-construction ecological checks and surveys.
Provide watching briefs during sensitive construction activities.
Monitor compliance with ecological mitigation requirements.
Identify emerging ecological risks and advise project teams on appropriate controls.
Establish and monitor ecological exclusion zones and buffers.
Stop, pause or escalate activities where there is an immediate risk of ecological harm or legal non-compliance.
Maintain accurate records of ecological inspections, observations and interventions.

Protected Species

Provide specialist advice and support relating to protected and notable species including, where relevant:

Otters.
Badgers.
Bats.
Red squirrels.
Pine martens.
Water voles.
Great crested newts.
Reptiles and amphibians.
Breeding birds.
Schedule 1 birds.
Raptors.
Freshwater pearl mussels.
Fish and aquatic ecology.
Invasive non-native species.
Other protected or priority species relevant to project locations.

Ensure works are undertaken in accordance with relevant licences and Species Protection Plans.

Surveys & Assessments

Undertake or coordinate Preliminary Ecological Appraisals.
Undertake habitat and protected species surveys within the individual's competence.
Support UKHab and other appropriate habitat classification and condition assessments.
Review ecological survey information provided by consultants.
Identify requirements for additional surveys or specialist ecological support.
Support ecological inputs into Environmental Impact Assessments and project environmental documentation.

Construction Support

Review RAMS and construction methodologies for ecological risks.
Provide ecological input into Construction Environmental Management Plans.
Develop and implement Species Protection Plans and ecological mitigation measures.
Undertake pre-start ecological briefings and toolbox talks.
Provide practical ecological advice to Site Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and subcontractors.
Attend planning and construction meetings where ecological constraints could affect delivery.

Sensitive Habitats & Peatland

Support the protection and management of sensitive Scottish habitats including:

Peatland and deep peat.
Blanket bog.
Wet heath.
Ancient woodland.
Native woodland.
Riparian habitats.
Freshwater environments.
Protected and designated sites.

Support implementation and monitoring of habitat and peatland restoration and reinstatement requirements.

Designated Sites

Provide ecological support for projects potentially affecting:

Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs).
Special Areas of Conservation (SACs).
Special Protection Areas (SPAs).
Ramsar sites.
National Nature Reserves.
Ancient Woodland.
Local Nature Conservation Sites.

Ensure project teams understand and implement controls associated with designated sites.

Biodiversity & Habitat Enhancement

Support delivery of project biodiversity objectives.
Identify opportunities for habitat enhancement and restoration.
Monitor habitat reinstatement following construction.
Support biodiversity monitoring programmes.
Assist with development and implementation of Biodiversity Enhancement Plans and client commitments.
Maintain evidence demonstrating delivery of ecological mitigation and enhancement measures.

Environmental Compliance

Provide ecological advice relating to applicable Scottish requirements including:

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004.
Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.
Conservation (Natural Habitats, &c.) Regulations 1994, as amended.
Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
Environmental Authorisation (Scotland) Regulations 2018, where relevant.
Applicable planning conditions, licences, consents and client requirements.

Maintain awareness of legislative changes and guidance affecting ecological management in Scotland.

Ecological Incidents

Respond to ecological incidents and unexpected discoveries.
Immediately advise project teams where protected species or previously unidentified ecological constraints are encountered.
Support environmental incident investigations.
Escalate significant issues to the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager.
Support liaison with statutory bodies where required.
Capture and communicate lessons learned.

Stakeholder Engagement

Develop effective relationships with clients, project teams, landowners, ecological consultants, local authorities and statutory bodies including NatureScot, SEPA and relevant planning authorities.

Represent the project at ecological and environmental meetings as required.

Reporting & Assurance

Produce ecological inspection and monitoring reports.
Maintain ecological constraints registers.
Maintain records of licences, mitigation and monitoring requirements.
Track ecological actions through to closure.
Provide ecological information for project SHEQ reports.
Support environmental audits and client assurance visits.
Maintain auditable evidence demonstrating compliance with ecological commitments.

Key Accountabilities

The role is accountable for:

Effective management of ecological risks across project activities.
Competent delivery of the ECoW function.
Compliance with protected species legislation and licences.
Protection of sensitive habitats and designated sites.
Implementation of Species Protection Plans.
Accurate and timely ecological records.
Effective escalation of significant ecological risks.
Supporting habitat restoration and biodiversity commitments.
Prevention of avoidable ecological harm.

Essential Qualifications

Degree or equivalent qualification in Ecology, Environmental Science, Conservation Biology or a related discipline.
Appropriate membership of CIEEM or equivalent professional body.
Strong working knowledge of Scottish ecological legislation and protected species requirements.
Full UK Driving Licence.

Desirable Qualifications

Associate or Full Membership of CIEEM.
Protected species licences relevant to Scottish infrastructure projects.
CSCS/ECS or equivalent construction site competence.
ECoW training or demonstrable equivalent experience.
UKHab training.
Peatland assessment/restoration experience.
Environmental auditing qualification.

Essential Experience

Practical ecological experience within construction, utilities, infrastructure or a similar sector.
Experience undertaking ecological surveys and site inspections.
Experience working as an ECoW or providing equivalent construction-phase ecological support.
Strong knowledge of protected species and habitat management.
Ability to interpret ecological reports, Species Protection Plans and licence conditions.
Experience communicating ecological requirements to construction teams.

Desirable Experience

Power Transmission & Distribution projects.
Overhead line, underground cable and substation construction.
Major infrastructure projects in the Scottish Highlands and remote environments.
SSEN Transmission or SP Energy Networks projects.
Experience working around peatland, forestry and watercourses.
Experience working within or adjacent to internationally and nationally designated sites.
Experience managing ecological interfaces across geographically dispersed construction work fronts.

Skills & Competencies

Strong field ecology capability.
Excellent understanding of Scottish protected species requirements.
Ability to translate ecological requirements into practical construction controls.
Strong communication and influencing skills.
Confidence to challenge or stop activities where ecological harm may occur.
Strong technical reporting and record keeping.
Ability to work independently in remote and challenging environments.
Collaborative and solutions-focused approach.

Values & Behaviours

The Ecologist / ECoW will demonstrate professional integrity, sound ecological judgement and visible environmental leadership. They will work collaboratively with project teams to enable successful infrastructure delivery while ensuring Scotland's habitats, species and natural environment are appropriately protected.

The role holder will be fully empowered and expected to challenge, pause or stop activities where there is a foreseeable risk of significant ecological harm, breach of licence conditions or environmental non-compliance

jobs.title: Research Scientist and Project Director - College of Engineering - Environmental and Public Policy
jobs.description:
Carnegie Mellon University is a private, global research university that stands among the world’s most renowned education institutions. With ground-breaking brain science, path-breaking performances, creative start-ups, big data, big ambitions, hands-on learning, and a whole lot of robots, CMU doesn’t imagine the future, we invent it. If you’re passionate about joining a community that challenges the curious to deliver work that matters, your journey starts here!

The Department of Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is a unique department in the College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University which addresses important problems in technology and policy. We educate technically skilled students to be leaders in policy-focused research; we work on policy problems in which the technology matters.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks a Research Scientist to serve as Project Director for Industrial Futures within the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. The position will lead research and programmatic activities at the intersection of industrial transformation, energy and climate, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, and regional economic development. The Research Scientist will lead the Industrial Futures focus area within the Scott Institute, working with faculty, researchers, students, and external partners across Carnegie Mellon and a network of domestic and international collaborators. The position

combines applied and scholarly research with project leadership, external engagement, policy communication, and mentorship. The Research Scientist will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

A central objective of the Industrial Futures initiative is to understand how technological change and the energy transition reshaping industry, firms, workers, and regions are — and how policy, innovation, and entrepreneurship can contribute to competitive, resilient, and sustainable industrial transitions. The portfolio connects research and engagement in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with international

research and partnerships addressing similar challenges around the world.

The Research Scientist will have substantial responsibility for two major components of this portfolio: CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, an international research collaboration focused on industrial transformation and decarbonization, and its links to CMU’s engagement in the Regional Technology and Infrastructure Consortium (RETI), which focuses on industrial innovation, hardtech entrepreneurship, and supporting policies. As Project Director, the Research Scientist will help shape the intellectual agenda of these initiatives while managing research programs, coordinating partners, developing new projects, and translating research findings for policy and practitioner audiences.

Core Responsibilities

Research Leadership:

Develop, lead, and contribute to applied research on industrial transformation, energy and industrial policy, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and regional economic change.
Help define and advance the research agenda for the Industrial Futures focus area and lead or co-lead projects from research design through analysis, publication, and dissemination.
Conduct rigorous quantitative and qualitative research using methods appropriate to the research question, including quantitative empirical analysis, operations research, econometrics, labor-market and regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based research, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Maintain and develop datasets, analytical tools, and methodological frameworks that support research across multiple projects.
Develop and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, policy reports, working papers, and other scholarly outputs.
Collaborate with researchers across Carnegie Mellon and partner institutions, connecting research on industrial transformation in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with related international research and identifying opportunities for new interdisciplinary work.

Program And Project Leadership

Serve as Project Director for the Industrial Futures portfolio, providing intellectual and programmatic leadership across its research and engagement activities.
Coordinate complex, multi-institution research projects, including developing and reviewing deliverables, maintaining timelines, leading project meetings, monitoring progress, and addressing barriers to project success.
Serve as a primary point of contact for research partners, subcontractors, funding organizations, and other collaborators.
Support CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, including coordinating research across partner institutions, managing a collaborative seed-grant program, and leading knowledge-sharing activities such as newsletters, workshops, and study tours.
Coordinate project reporting and communications with research sponsors and contribute to new grant proposals, including research design, technical narratives, work plans, and partnership development.
Connect researchers across the Scott Institute and broader university who are working on related topics or methodologies and facilitate opportunities for collaboration.

External Engagement And Policy Impact

Build and maintain relationships with industry, government, nonprofit and community organizations, research institutions, funding partners, and other stakeholders.
Engage with firms, policymakers, entrepreneurs, workforce organizations, and regional stakeholders to understand the opportunities and challenges associated with industrial and technological transformation.
Represent Carnegie Mellon and the Scott Institute in external meetings, workshops, conferences, study tours, working groups, and other convenings.
Translate research into accessible and decision-relevant formats, including policy briefs, reports, presentations, data visualizations, and other communications for policymakers and practitioners.
Work with Scott Institute communications and policy staff to disseminate research findings and contribute to policy-informing activities such as briefings, testimony, public comments, and workshops.

Advising And Mentorship

Advise or co-advise student and researcher projects associated with the Industrial Futures portfolio.
Mentor students and junior researchers on research design, quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis and visualization, and research writing.
Provide feedback on research products, manuscripts, presentations, and policy communications.
Contribute to a collaborative, intellectually engaged, productive, and supportive research culture within the Scott Institute and collaborating research groups.

Adaptability, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. We are in search of a team member who can effectively interact with a varied population of internal and external partners at a high level of integrity. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work

Qualifications

Ph.D. in engineering, public policy, economics, management, or a related field.
Approximately 3–5 years of relevant research or professional experience. Significant and directly relevant research, project leadership, or stakeholder- engagement experience obtained during doctoral training may count toward this requirement.
Demonstrated research experience in one or more of the following areas: energy, industrial transformation, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, or regional economic development.
Demonstrated ability to design and conduct rigorous applied research using multiple quantitative and/or qualitative approaches. Relevant methods may include quantitative empirical research, operations research, econometrics, labor-market or regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based methods, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex datasets using R, Python, Stata, or comparable analytical software.
Experience developing scholarly research products, including peer-reviewed publications, working papers, or major research reports.
Strong project-management and organizational skills and the ability to coordinate activities and collaborators across complex projects.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical research to academic and nonacademic audiences.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across disciplines and institutions.
A combination of education and relevant experience from which comparable knowledge is demonstrated may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Research or professional experience related to industrial decarbonization, industrial or energy policy, hardtech innovation and entrepreneurship, or regional industrial transformation.
Experience working at the intersection of academic research and policy or practice and engaging directly with industry, government, community organizations, or other external stakeholders.
Experience managing multi-institutional or interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Experience developing research proposals or contributing to externally funded research programs.
Experience translating academic research into policy-relevant communications for nonacademic audiences.
Experience mentoring students or junior researchers.
Experience working in international research collaborations or comparative research settings.

Requirements

Successful background check

Position Characteristics

This position is designed for a researcher who enjoys moving between rigorous research and real-world engagement. The successful candidate will be comfortable leading research while also building partnerships, managing collaborative projects, mentoring students, communicating findings to policymakers and practitioners, and developing new research opportunities.

The role requires intellectual curiosity, independence, initiative, strong organizational skills, and a collaborative approach. Because the Industrial Futures portfolio connects local, national, and international research and engagement, the position may involve periodic domestic and international travel.

The Research Scientist will be based at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

Work arrangement:
In-person expected

Benefits eligible employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance as well as a generous retirement savings program with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our Family Concierge Team to help navigate childcare needs, fitness center access, and much more!

For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our Benefits page.

We appreciate your unique skills and the perspective you bring. Your journey with us is about more than just a job; it’s about finding the perfect fit for your professional growth and personal aspirations.

Description

About You

You are an experienced environmental chemist or scientist with experience reviewing and validating environmental data and supporting field programs. You are a strategic thinker who thrives on the challenges of these complex, interdisciplinary environment matters. A lifelong learner, you want to keep growing intellectually and professionally. Collaborating with colleagues with diverse expertise is exciting for you, and you are also comfortable working independently. Quality management and integrity are among your strongest principles.

About Integral

Integral Consulting Inc. is a science and engineering firm delivering sound technical solutions to meet today’s challenges in the health, environmental, and natural resource arenas. We are a values-driven collaborative team that is as passionate about company culture as we are about the work we do for our clients. Since our founding in 2002, we have operated with a demonstrated commitment to the well-being, diversity, and professional development of our staff and an equal commitment to strong partnerships with our clients and teaming partners. We are a company where people come to solve today’s toughest environmental challenges through innovative ideas, exceptional teamwork, and dedication to accuracy and technical quality.

About The Job

We are currently seeking a chemist with 3 to 5 years of experience who has the desire to also do some field work with our Sediment and Water Investigations and Monitoring practice in our Santa Cruz, California office. The position supports multiple clients and projects, with day-to-day responsibilities that primarily include reviewing and validating of laboratory data, managing a small wet laboratory, supporting field efforts, and on occasion performing some fieldwork. The selected candidate will work closely with project team members on water quality monitoring, stormwater planning and monitoring, and sediment sampling efforts across the Bay Area and Northern California.

This position is primarily in-office, but opportunities for hybrid work may be available.

Requirements

Responsibilities

As a Scientist, your job functions will include, but not be limited to:

Assisting with sample control procedures for multiple projects
Tracking submission of samples to chemistry laboratories and receipt of associated data for multiple projects
Adhering quality control and quality assurance procedures to ensure data integrity
Communicating with laboratories regarding data quality questions or corrections that may be needed.
Performing quality assurance reviews of technical analyses and results
Managing laboratory and data validation subcontractors
Reviewing CEDEN EDDs and applying the Quality Assurance codes associated with chemistry excursions
Performing Stage 2B and Stage 3 data validation and reporting following EPA’s National Functional Guidelines
Assisting in writing formal QAQC reports
Executing laboratory bottle cleaning procedures and maintaining facility organization
Managing and maintaining a small wet laboratory
Collecting river, stream, creek, ocean, and stormwater samples
Collecting sediment and surface water samples both on land and from boats
Maintaining accurate field and laboratory logs
Adhering to company, project, state, and federal safety policies

Fieldwork will occasionally be required; those responsibilities may include long days in the field, extended exposure to the elements (sun, rain, wind), prolonged standing, and other physically demanding tasks such as lifting equipment or materials. You must have the ability and willingness to work outdoors in a wide range of weather conditions. Your work schedule at times will be defined by storm forecasts and may include working nights and/or weekends.

Qualifications

Candidates should hold at a minimum, a B.A. or B.S. in chemistry or a related science and have at least 3 years of experience in a related technical field.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have

Familiarity with environmental analytical methods for water and sediments
Demonstrated strong personal initiative towards projects, critical thinking, and problem solving
Solid attention to detail
Ability to oversee a small wet laboratory, cleaning glassware and field equipment
Flexibility with work hours as required to meet project needs
Affinity for working outdoors in all weather conditions, with some nights and weekends
A valid U.S. driver's license (or ability to obtain one upon hire) and a clean driving record. If a driver’s license cannot be obtained, reliable transportation to project and field sites is required
Ability to lift and carry items of varying weights as required by the job, occasionally up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation
Proficiency with Microsoft® Office products Word and Excel
Excellent written and oral communication skills
A desire to grow both intellectually and professionally
Strong organizational abilities
Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers

Compensation is commensurate with experience and internal equity, within the listed range. An employee’s total compensation package includes annual salary, company-subsidized (employee and family) medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) participation with a company match of 1% to 4% of annual compensation, company-paid life and short- and long-term disability insurance, paid sick leave (10 days), paid vacation (12 days;), and paid holidays (9 days) per year, and the potential for an annual discretionary bonus based on company performance. Paid time off will be prorated to reflect part-time scheduled hours, if applicable.

Role description

Under direction, the 6120 Consumer Protection Environmental Health Inspector conducts inspections of housing, industrial plants and premises, solid waste facilities and vehicles, sources of noise emission, fixed and mobile food facilities, and public health and safety hazards in order to enforce established laws, ordinances and regulations pertaining to abatement of violations found; recommends appropriate actions to remedy situations; issues citations; prepares pertinent reports; implements various environmental health programs and services; and performs related duties as required.

Enforces provisions of the health, housing, planning and air pollution codes; State health and safety, industrial relations, administrative, agricultural and penal codes, State general safety orders, and sanitary aspects of meat plant construction, local ordinances and noise abatement and other environmental hazards; may be required to specialize in any of these or other activities related to the duties of the class.

Applications will be reviewed regularly, and interviews may be conducted prior to the application close date.

As a Senior Environmental Program Manager, you will lead the day-to-day management and compliance of National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES), King County Industrial Waste Discharge, and support other stormwater elements for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You will lead staff members to provide technical oversight of field monitoring, inspection, documentation, contract management and reporting. The position requires complex program implementation as well as environmental program development in response to new and changing regulations, environmental goals and Airport operations.

You will lead and define both the long-term and short-term stormwater strategies related to planning, implementation and oversight of SEA’s stormwater management programs, including maintaining compliance with industrial stormwater permits, stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPP), stormwater monitoring, best management practices, and water quality improvement initiatives.
You will serve as SEA’s technical expert on stormwater regulations and water quality requirements, providing guidance on the SEA NPDES permit, Washington State stormwater regulations, Clean Water Act requirements and emerging regulatory issues affecting airport operations.
You will provide strategic and technical leadership during planning, design, and construction of airport capital projects by reviewing stormwater infrastructure, drainage design, treatment systems, construction activities, and operational impacts to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and Port policies.
You will negotiate strategic and technical requirements and compliance strategies with regulatory agencies, airport tenants, consultants, contractors and internal departments while representing SEA during inspections, permit discussions, audits, enforcement matters and interagency coordination efforts.
You will manage consultant contracts and outside technical services supporting stormwater planning, engineering evaluations, monitoring, modeling, regulatory compliance and implementation of stormwater improvement projects. You will develop scope of work, budget, schedule and performance requirements while reviewing and approving technical deliverables.
You will act as a key member of the environmental spill team, responsible for responding by vehicle to incidents at the airport, monitoring spill response, directing cleaning resources and providing input on impacted stormwater resources.
You will supervise a team of up to 3 stormwater professionals, responsible for all aspects of development, performance and evaluation.

Who you are:

Experienced – You have five (5) years of experience in environmental and/or sustainability, to include two (2) years of lead, mentor or supervisory experience including leading a project or process.
Desired – We hope you have a bachelor’s degree in environmental science or environmental engineering, civil engineering or a related discipline. We hope you have certifications such as a Professional Engineer (PE), Licensed HydroGeologist (LHG), Certified Professional in Stormwater Quality (CPSWQ), Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC).
Committed to Equity – You will apply equity and exemplify shared values, behaviors, and practices in all aspects of the work. At the Port of Seattle, equity is a daily responsibility and a foundational expectation for all Port employees.
Technical Expert – You possess recognized expertise in stormwater management principles, hydrology, drainage systems, stormwater treatment technologies, water quality monitoring and environmental compliance practices. You have extensive knowledge of stormwater regulations, including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES) permitting requirements, Clean Water Act regulations, Washington State stormwater requirements and related environmental standards. You have knowledge of airport, industrial, transportation or other highly regulated environmental programs.
Efficient Communicator – You have proven effective verbal and written communication skills and are adept at communicating complex technical, regulatory and environmental information to diverse audiences including executives, regulators, airport tenants, contractors, consultants elected officials and the public. You have proven negotiation, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, as well as experience building and maintaining effective relationships with regulators.
Leader – You can effectively lead multidisciplinary people and project teams on complex environmental programs while collaborating with airport operations, engineering, maintenance, planning, tenants, consultants, and regulatory agencies. You understand how operational requirements, regulatory obligations, emerging environmental issues, and community expectations influence airport decision-making.
Analytical Problem-Solver – You can analyze complex stormwater and environmental challenges, analyze technical data, interpret changing regulations, and develop strategic, innovative, and practical solutions. You can identify compliance risks, recommend improvements, and support decisions affecting airport infrastructure, operations, and long-term environmental performance.

What Else You Need To Know

Driver’s License – You will need a valid Washington State Driver’s License, or the ability to obtain one, is required in order to travel locally to project sites.
Work Schedule – Your normal work schedule will be Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (40 hours per week). Slightly more flexible start and end times are available in this role. You may be required to work any and all assigned shifts, including weekends and holidays. You will have a rotation responsibility (approximately 7 weeks per calendar year) for 24 hours on call spill response and may be required to work during emergencies.
Work Environment – This is a field-based position. You will work throughout Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), maritime facilities, and other Port of Seattle properties, with occasional work in an office setting for administrative tasks, meetings, or training.
Washington State Residency Requirement – Employees must establish a residence in Washington state within 30 days of their first day of employment and must maintain a residence in Washington State during their employment with the Port of Seattle. If a position is eligible to telework, work performed while teleworking must be performed in Washington State.
Security Requirements – As the successful candidate, you must pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check as well as a criminal history background check with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Your employment will be contingent upon obtaining a Port of Seattle ID badge upon clearance.

Every role at the Port of Seattle is vital to our thriving community. We are a leader in moving people and cargo across the country and around the world. Reporting To:
SHEQ Manager

Location:

Function:
SHEQ / Environment

Role Purpose

The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Scotland.

Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with Scottish environmental legislation, planning requirements, protected species licences, client requirements and project environmental commitments.

The role will have a strong field-based component, working alongside project management, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological constraints, develop practical mitigation and provide ECoW supervision of activities in environmentally sensitive locations.

The position will be particularly important on linear power infrastructure projects where construction activities may interact with protected species, designated sites, peatland, watercourses, forestry and sensitive habitats.

Key Responsibilities

Ecological Clerk of Works

Act as ECoW for construction activities requiring ecological supervision.
Undertake pre-construction ecological checks and surveys.
Provide watching briefs during sensitive construction activities.
Monitor compliance with ecological mitigation requirements.
Identify emerging ecological risks and advise project teams on appropriate controls.
Establish and monitor ecological exclusion zones and buffers.
Stop, pause or escalate activities where there is an immediate risk of ecological harm or legal non-compliance.
Maintain accurate records of ecological inspections, observations and interventions.

Protected Species

Provide specialist advice and support relating to protected and notable species including, where relevant:

Otters.
Badgers.
Bats.
Red squirrels.
Pine martens.
Water voles.
Great crested newts.
Reptiles and amphibians.
Breeding birds.
Schedule 1 birds.
Raptors.
Freshwater pearl mussels.
Fish and aquatic ecology.
Invasive non-native species.
Other protected or priority species relevant to project locations.

Ensure works are undertaken in accordance with relevant licences and Species Protection Plans.

Surveys & Assessments

Undertake or coordinate Preliminary Ecological Appraisals.
Undertake habitat and protected species surveys within the individual's competence.
Support UKHab and other appropriate habitat classification and condition assessments.
Review ecological survey information provided by consultants.
Identify requirements for additional surveys or specialist ecological support.
Support ecological inputs into Environmental Impact Assessments and project environmental documentation.

Construction Support

Review RAMS and construction methodologies for ecological risks.
Provide ecological input into Construction Environmental Management Plans.
Develop and implement Species Protection Plans and ecological mitigation measures.
Undertake pre-start ecological briefings and toolbox talks.
Provide practical ecological advice to Site Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and subcontractors.
Attend planning and construction meetings where ecological constraints could affect delivery.

Sensitive Habitats & Peatland

Support the protection and management of sensitive Scottish habitats including:

Peatland and deep peat.
Blanket bog.
Wet heath.
Ancient woodland.
Native woodland.
Riparian habitats.
Freshwater environments.
Protected and designated sites.

Support implementation and monitoring of habitat and peatland restoration and reinstatement requirements.

Designated Sites

Provide ecological support for projects potentially affecting:

Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs).
Special Areas of Conservation (SACs).
Special Protection Areas (SPAs).
Ramsar sites.
National Nature Reserves.
Ancient Woodland.
Local Nature Conservation Sites.

Ensure project teams understand and implement controls associated with designated sites.

Biodiversity & Habitat Enhancement

Support delivery of project biodiversity objectives.
Identify opportunities for habitat enhancement and restoration.
Monitor habitat reinstatement following construction.
Support biodiversity monitoring programmes.
Assist with development and implementation of Biodiversity Enhancement Plans and client commitments.
Maintain evidence demonstrating delivery of ecological mitigation and enhancement measures.

Environmental Compliance

Provide ecological advice relating to applicable Scottish requirements including:

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004.
Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.
Conservation (Natural Habitats, &c.) Regulations 1994, as amended.
Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
Environmental Authorisation (Scotland) Regulations 2018, where relevant.
Applicable planning conditions, licences, consents and client requirements.

Maintain awareness of legislative changes and guidance affecting ecological management in Scotland.

Ecological Incidents

Respond to ecological incidents and unexpected discoveries.
Immediately advise project teams where protected species or previously unidentified ecological constraints are encountered.
Support environmental incident investigations.
Escalate significant issues to the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager.
Support liaison with statutory bodies where required.
Capture and communicate lessons learned.

Stakeholder Engagement

Develop effective relationships with clients, project teams, landowners, ecological consultants, local authorities and statutory bodies including NatureScot, SEPA and relevant planning authorities.

Represent the project at ecological and environmental meetings as required.

Reporting & Assurance

Produce ecological inspection and monitoring reports.
Maintain ecological constraints registers.
Maintain records of licences, mitigation and monitoring requirements.
Track ecological actions through to closure.
Provide ecological information for project SHEQ reports.
Support environmental audits and client assurance visits.
Maintain auditable evidence demonstrating compliance with ecological commitments.

Key Accountabilities

The role is accountable for:

Effective management of ecological risks across project activities.
Competent delivery of the ECoW function.
Compliance with protected species legislation and licences.
Protection of sensitive habitats and designated sites.
Implementation of Species Protection Plans.
Accurate and timely ecological records.
Effective escalation of significant ecological risks.
Supporting habitat restoration and biodiversity commitments.
Prevention of avoidable ecological harm.

Essential Qualifications

Degree or equivalent qualification in Ecology, Environmental Science, Conservation Biology or a related discipline.
Appropriate membership of CIEEM or equivalent professional body.
Strong working knowledge of Scottish ecological legislation and protected species requirements.
Full UK Driving Licence.

Protected species licences relevant to Scottish infrastructure projects.
CSCS/ECS or equivalent construction site competence.
ECoW training or demonstrable equivalent experience.

Peatland assessment/restoration experience.
Environmental auditing qualification.

Essential Experience

Experience undertaking ecological surveys and site inspections.
Experience working as an ECoW or providing equivalent construction-phase ecological support.
Strong knowledge of protected species and habitat management.
Ability to interpret ecological reports, Species Protection Plans and licence conditions.

Major infrastructure projects in the Scottish Highlands and remote environments.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks a Research Scientist to serve as Project Director for Industrial Futures within the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. The Research Scientist will lead the Industrial Futures focus area within the Scott Institute, working with faculty, researchers, students, and external partners across Carnegie Mellon and a network of domestic and international collaborators. The position

combines applied and scholarly research with project leadership, external engagement, policy communication, and mentorship. The Research Scientist will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

A central objective of the Industrial Futures initiative is to understand how technological change and the energy transition reshaping industry, firms, workers, and regions are — and how policy, innovation, and entrepreneurship can contribute to competitive, resilient, and sustainable industrial transitions. The portfolio connects research and engagement in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with international

research and partnerships addressing similar challenges around the world.

The Research Scientist will have substantial responsibility for two major components of this portfolio: CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, an international research collaboration focused on industrial transformation and decarbonization, and its links to CMU’s engagement in the Regional Technology and Infrastructure Consortium (RETI), which focuses on industrial innovation, hardtech entrepreneurship, and supporting policies. Develop, lead, and contribute to applied research on industrial transformation, energy and industrial policy, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and regional economic change.

Serve as a primary point of contact for research partners, subcontractors, funding organizations, and other collaborators.

Coordinate project reporting and communications with research sponsors and contribute to new grant proposals, including research design, technical narratives, work plans, and partnership development.
Connect researchers across the Scott Institute and broader university who are working on related topics or methodologies and facilitate opportunities for collaboration.

External Engagement And Policy Impact

Build and maintain relationships with industry, government, nonprofit and community organizations, research institutions, funding partners, and other stakeholders.
Engage with firms, policymakers, entrepreneurs, workforce organizations, and regional stakeholders to understand the opportunities and challenges associated with industrial and technological transformation.
Represent Carnegie Mellon and the Scott Institute in external meetings, workshops, conferences, study tours, working groups, and other convenings.
Translate research into accessible and decision-relevant formats, including policy briefs, reports, presentations, data visualizations, and other communications for policymakers and practitioners.

Mentor students and junior researchers on research design, quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis and visualization, and research writing.
Provide feedback on research products, manuscripts, presentations, and policy communications.

We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work

We are currently seeking a chemist with 3 to 5 years of experience who has the desire to also do some field work with our Sediment and Water Investigations and Monitoring practice in our Santa Cruz, California office. The position supports multiple clients and projects, with day-to-day responsibilities that primarily include reviewing and validating of laboratory data, managing a small wet laboratory, supporting field efforts, and on occasion performing some fieldwork. As a Senior Environmental Program Manager, you will lead the day-to-day management and compliance of National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES), King County Industrial Waste Discharge, and support other stormwater elements for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You will lead staff members to provide technical oversight of field monitoring, inspection, documentation, contract management and reporting. The position requires complex program implementation as well as environmental program development in response to new and changing regulations, environmental goals and Airport operations.

You will lead and define both the long-term and short-term stormwater strategies related to planning, implementation and oversight of SEA’s stormwater management programs, including maintaining compliance with industrial stormwater permits, stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPP), stormwater monitoring, best management practices, and water quality improvement initiatives.
You will serve as SEA’s technical expert on stormwater regulations and water quality requirements, providing guidance on the SEA NPDES permit, Washington State stormwater regulations, Clean Water Act requirements and emerging regulatory issues affecting airport operations.
You will provide strategic and technical leadership during planning, design, and construction of airport capital projects by reviewing stormwater infrastructure, drainage design, treatment systems, construction activities, and operational impacts to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and Port policies.
You will negotiate strategic and technical requirements and compliance strategies with regulatory agencies, airport tenants, consultants, contractors and internal departments while representing SEA during inspections, permit discussions, audits, enforcement matters and interagency coordination efforts.
You will manage consultant contracts and outside technical services supporting stormwater planning, engineering evaluations, monitoring, modeling, regulatory compliance and implementation of stormwater improvement projects. You will develop scope of work, budget, schedule and performance requirements while reviewing and approving technical deliverables.
You will act as a key member of the environmental spill team, responsible for responding by vehicle to incidents at the airport, monitoring spill response, directing cleaning resources and providing input on impacted stormwater resources.
You will supervise a team of up to 3 stormwater professionals, responsible for all aspects of development, performance and evaluation.

Experienced – You have five (5) years of experience in environmental and/or sustainability, to include two (2) years of lead, mentor or supervisory experience including leading a project or process.
Desired – We hope you have a bachelor’s degree in environmental science or environmental engineering, civil engineering or a related discipline. We hope you have certifications such as a Professional Engineer (PE), Licensed HydroGeologist (LHG), Certified Professional in Stormwater Quality (CPSWQ), Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC).

Technical Expert – You possess recognized expertise in stormwater management principles, hydrology, drainage systems, stormwater treatment technologies, water quality monitoring and environmental compliance practices. You have extensive knowledge of stormwater regulations, including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES) permitting requirements, Clean Water Act regulations, Washington State stormwater requirements and related environmental standards. You have knowledge of airport, industrial, transportation or other highly regulated environmental programs.
Efficient Communicator – You have proven effective verbal and written communication skills and are adept at communicating complex technical, regulatory and environmental information to diverse audiences including executives, regulators, airport tenants, contractors, consultants elected officials and the public. You have proven negotiation, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, as well as experience building and maintaining effective relationships with regulators.
Leader – You can effectively lead multidisciplinary people and project teams on complex environmental programs while collaborating with airport operations, engineering, maintenance, planning, tenants, consultants, and regulatory agencies. You understand how operational requirements, regulatory obligations, emerging environmental issues, and community expectations influence airport decision-making.
Analytical Problem-Solver – You can analyze complex stormwater and environmental challenges, analyze technical data, interpret changing regulations, and develop strategic, innovative, and practical solutions. You can identify compliance risks, recommend improvements, and support decisions affecting airport infrastructure, operations, and long-term environmental performance.

Summary Of Job Description

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.
Serve as primary client/agency interface (USACE/USEPA as applicable); communicate progress, risks, and issues to stakeholders and executive management; resolve disputes professionally and promptly.
Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Knowledge & Tools

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. As a $100 M small business, we have Nationwide contracts with the USACE, USN and USAF totaling over $20 B in prime contract capacity. As a top 3 SB in our industry, our $12 B portfolio also includes unrestricted contracts where we compete against large businesses for task order awards. Most recently in the unrestricted area, CAPE won a $30 M + groundwater treatment plant construction project for the USACE in New Jersey. We routinely partner with other small and large businesses to provide better responsiveness in support of achieving our clients’ goals.

Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals and employee’s professional goals and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, Vanguard retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home.
